companyDescription: Satellite broadband · Direct-to-cell 4G/5G via LEO satellites — smartphones connect without towers
priceNote: Aug 3 close · ↑7.7% pre-launch rally — market pricing in Aug 5 BlueBird 11/12/13 launch (3:42am EDT, Falcon 9, Cape Canaveral); down from $133 ATH (May 28) but well off the $55.74 Aug 3 intraday low
summary: ASTS rallied +7.7% into the Aug 5 launch of next-gen BlueBird 11/12/13 (nearly 2x peak download speed vs Block 1), the next binary catalyst after the Jun 17 BB8/9/10 success. Wall Street has turned more constructive: Piper Sandler initiated Overweight ($100 PT, calling ASTS the best risk/reward of the space names), B. Riley upgraded to Buy ($85), even Scotiabank flipped from Underperform to Sector Perform ($50.80). Q2 2026 revenue guidance reaffirmed at $150-200M with $1.2B+ contracted backlog from ~60 MNOs including AT&T/Verizon, targeting ~45 satellites and ~$1B revenue run rate by 2027. Offsetting: a $1.15B convertible note (due 2034, priced Jul 21) raised near-term dilution/leverage questions even as the capped call caps effective dilution under 2%, and the Fed's hawkish June dot plot (rates on hold, hike risk flagged) keeps growth-stock valuations under pressure. Q2 earnings (~Aug 10-14) is the next dated catalyst after launch. Still binary, still pre-profit — size as ค่าขนม only.

catalysts.name: BlueBird 11/12/13 Launch
catalysts.description: SpaceX Falcon 9 from Cape Canaveral, liftoff targeted 3:42am EDT (backup 5:10am). Next-gen stackable architecture, nearly 2x peak download speed vs Block 1 (which hit 98.9 Mbps). Pushes constellation toward the ~45-satellite year-end target.

catalysts.name: Q2 2026 Earnings
catalysts.description: Expected ~Aug 10-14 (date not yet confirmed by company). Market watching: commercial activation progress with AT&T/Verizon, revenue trajectory toward the $150-200M FY26 guide, and constellation build-out update post-launch.

catalysts.name: Japan J-LEO Award — Binary Event
catalysts.description: Multi-billion JPY contract with Rakuten/NTT Docomo, decision still expected Q3 2026. Win = re-rate higher, miss = sharp drawdown. Remains the biggest single binary swing factor for H2 2026.

risks: Still binary/pre-profit — $150-200M FY26 revenue guide vs $24.65B market cap; execution risk on scaling from ~10 to 45 satellites remains untested at this pace

$1.15B convertible notes due 2034 (closed Jul 21) — stock fell as much as 13% after-hours on the initial offering announcement (Jul 15) before recovering; leverage now on the balance sheet even with capped-call dilution protection (<2% effective)

Analyst split remains wide — targets range from Scotiabank's $50.80 (Sector Perform, still below spot at times) to Piper Sandler's $100 (Overweight); consensus rating is still net Hold/Neutral, not broad Buy
Fed dot plot turned hawkish in June (rates held 3.50-3.75%, some members flagging hike risk) — pressures long-duration/pre-profit growth names broadly
SpaceX Starlink Direct-to-Cell (T-Mobile) competition — head start on satellite count and a much larger balance sheet
Japan J-LEO binary risk still unresolved — a miss would remove the main H2 2026 re-rate catalyst
Launch-day execution risk — any anomaly on Aug 5 (weather scrub, vehicle issue, deployment failure) would hit sentiment hard given the stock already ran +7.7% into it

estimateDates.note: Falcon 9 from Cape Canaveral — next-gen satellites, ~2x peak speed vs Block 1
Commercial activation + AT&T/Verizon ramp read; FY26 $150-200M guide check-in
Binary event — Rakuten/NTT Docomo multi-billion JPY contract decision

macroRisk.rateOutlook: June FOMC held rates at 3.50-3.75% with a hawkish dot-plot shift — median 2026 year-end projection rose to 3.8%, and roughly half the committee flagged possible hikes rather than cuts. Markets that entered 2026 pricing cuts are now pricing higher-for-longer, or even tightening.
macroRisk.inflationNote: A higher-for-longer rate path raises the discount rate on ASTS's long-dated 2027+ revenue ramp and makes the newly issued $1.15B convertible debt costlier to refinance/service down the line, even at a low 1.625% coupon.
macroRisk.sectorImpact: Space/satellite names are more sensitive to risk-appetite and rate-driven multiple compression than to Fed policy directly — FCC spectrum decisions and launch-vehicle cadence (SpaceX/Falcon 9 availability) matter more day-to-day, but a hawkish macro backdrop caps how far pre-profit growth names can re-rate on good news.
macroRisk.summary: Macro risk MEDIUM (upgraded from LOW) — the June hawkish dot-plot shift matters more for a name that just raised $1.15B in convertible debt and won't be FCF-positive for years. Catalyst outcomes (launch, Japan) still dominate near-term price action, but macro is no longer a pure tailwind. Size accordingly: ค่าขนม only.

entryStrategy.verdict: SPECULATIVE — ค่าขนม only (max 3% of portfolio). Stock already ran +7.7% ahead of the Aug 5 launch; better to let the event pass and buy any post-launch pullback into $52-56 than chase here. Q2 earnings (~Aug 12) and Japan J-LEO (Q3) are the next two binary checkpoints — reassess sizing after each.

catalystSpot.preRunup: ASTS consistently runs up into scheduled launches — BB8/9/10 (Jun 17) saw the stock up ~5% on launch day itself after a volatile pre-launch drawdown; this cycle the stock is up +7.7% in the single session before the Aug 5 BB11/12/13 launch, on top of a string of analyst upgrades (Piper Sandler, B. Riley, Scotiabank) landing in the two weeks prior.
catalystSpot.preRunupTiming: 1-2 days immediately before a confirmed launch date, amplified by any analyst upgrades landing in the same window

postWin.note: BB1 (Apr 2024) ran +200%+ over the following 2 weeks after first direct-to-cell call confirmed. BB8/9/10 (Jun 17, 2026) added +5% same-day on successful deployment alone, before fading into July on macro/dilution news. Sector-wide consolidation news (Rocket Lab-Iridium deal, Jun 29 2026) also lifted ASTS +10% same-day purely on space-sector re-rating sentiment.

postLose.note: Blue Origin New Glenn hotfire explosion (May 29, 2026, a separate launch-partner risk) knocked ASTS -18% in a day. The $1B convertible note announcement (Jul 15, 2026) — dilution fear, not a launch failure — dropped shares -13% after-hours before recovering on completion.

spotSizing.reason: SPECULATIVE / ค่าขนม — binary Japan J-LEO still pending, stock already up +7.7% pre-launch so most of the immediate catalyst is priced in, wide analyst target dispersion ($51-$100). Max 3% of portfolio; do not add on launch-day spikes.

stopPreCatalyst.note: Break back below $54 before/around the Aug 5 launch would erase the pre-launch rally and signal the market doesn't believe the setup — reduce.

stopPostCatalyst.note: If the Aug 5 launch has any anomaly (scrub cascade, deployment issue) or Q2 earnings disappoint on commercial ramp, exit within 1-2 trading sessions — no revenue cushion yet to average through a thesis break.

comparableCases.event: Rocket Lab $8B acquisition announcement — space-sector consolidation
comparableCases.note: Iridium jumped ~20-25% in a day purely on being acquired at a premium; ASTS and Planet Labs also rose ~10% same-day on read-through consolidation/scarcity-value sentiment across the sector — shows how binary sector news can move ASTS even without a company-specific catalyst.

comparableCases.event: BlueBird 1 launch success + first direct-to-cell call
comparableCases.note: ASTS itself ran +100%+ over 2 weeks after BB1 confirmed the core direct-to-cell tech worked — the template bull case for what a flawless BB11/12/13 launch plus strong commercial ramp data could still do.

Shares fell 13% after-hours purely on dilution/leverage fear when the note offering was announced, even though the eventual terms (capped call, <2% effective dilution) were investor-friendly — shows the stock's sensitivity to financing headlines independent of operational news.
